assumptions: The NL states that there are twelve finite states but does not provide authoritative state names, so descriptive state names were synthesized from the twelve logical operating branches.

Because the NL describes states selected by current logical conditions over inputs, the model uses guarded forced transitions as a condition-classification abstraction rather than adding event/mode memory.

The NL does not provide complete numeric capacity variable names for every generator; Pd2max and Pbdismax were introduced to express DG2 and battery-discharge bounds needed by the stated priority and overload logic.
The relation between LNG and eng3_Pmax is interpreted as the LNG/engine capacity bound mentioned by the NL.

The PL = 0 and Ppv + Pw = 0 quiescent case is not represented as an additional state because the NL requires exactly twelve finite states and only describes PL = 0 behavior when RES production is sent to charging or spare.
Load cut-in/cut-out commands are declared and assigned, but detailed load-shedding behavior is abstracted because the NL does not specify load-priority thresholds or partial load groups.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, EMS serves demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Dispatch follows batteries when SoC is suitable, LNG before diesel units.
DG1/DG2 are only the last priority after RES, batteries, and LNG.
Extreme demand uses all thermal generating units; DG1/DG2 are last priority.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve Pd2max as an external input/read-only capacity bound; do not invent internal writes.
decisions.rationale: Pd2max is an external DG2 capacity bound used to classify dispatch branches. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds/resources; it does not define EMS-internal dynamics that update DG2 capacity. A DSL write would be a meaningless self-assignment or invented plant dynamics, so the safe repair is conservative preservation with explicit grounding rationale.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve Pbdismax as an external input/read-only capacity bound; do not invent internal writes.
decisions.rationale: Pbdismax is an external battery-discharge capacity bound needed by the NL priority logic. The NL does not specify EMS-internal update semantics for this bound. Adding a write would be ungrounded, so the safe repair is conservative preservation with explicit grounding rationale.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve BatteryOnly guard as an external-input logical selector.
decisions.rationale: The BatteryOnly selection guard reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbdismax, all of which are external demand/resource/battery-condition inputs in the NL. The guard is the required logical state selector and should not be simplified or replaced by invented updates.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve BatteryLng guard as an external-input logical selector.
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLng guard encodes the NL priority of RES, suitable battery discharge, then LNG before diesel using external inputs and capacity bounds. No NL-grounded internal writes exist for these inputs.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve BatteryLngDg1 guard as an external-input logical selector.
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLngDg1 guard is required to represent the later priority branch where DG1 is used after battery and LNG capacity are insufficient. Its variables are external inputs/capacity bounds, so adding writes would be ungrounded.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve AllThermalNormalSoc guard as an external-input logical selector.
decisions.rationale: The AllThermalNormalSoc guard uses external demand, renewable, battery, and thermal-capacity values to select the all-thermal normal-SoC branch. This is a required NL branch and should remain condition-driven.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc guard as an external-input logical selector.
decisions.rationale: The LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc guard represents the NL low-SoC diesel-generator case with Pd1max/10 charging margin and DG2 last priority. The read variables are external conditions/capacity bounds; internal writes would invent dynamics.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve OverloadCompletionIllegal guard as an external-input logical selector.
decisions.rationale: The OverloadCompletionIllegal guard is required by the NL to represent the illegal overload-completion branch where all thermal units are active and remaining lack is covered by battery discharge. Its inputs are external operating conditions/capacity bounds.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL text changed. The repair is a conservative design-level acceptance/grounding response: preserve external-input guards and read-only capacity bounds rather than adding ungrounded writes or deleting required twelve-state dispatch logic.

repair_rationale: No textual DSL edit is the smallest safe repair. The selected diagnostics are W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE on variables that the NL defines as read inputs: PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, engine/generator capacity bounds, and battery-discharge capacity.

The NL requires the twelve states to be selected by logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC. Replacing those guards with constants or removing them would delete required behavior.

Adding writes to Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, or Pd1max would invent plant/environment dynamics that the NL does not provide and is specifically forbidden by the repair request guidance.

All required preserved states, variables, and key selection transitions remain represented. The model remains a guarded condition-classifier EMS over externally supplied operating conditions and writes only EMS outputs/commands.

evidence.summary: The NL defines this EMS as a condition-classification FSM that reads external load demand PL, renewable inputs Ppv and Pw, SoC, and engine/generator capacity bounds, then selects one of twelve logical dispatch states. The candidate preserves all twelve required states, the required variables, the required forced selection guards, and the required dispatch actions/commands.

The complete FixLog shows SL-9 accepted all 12 design requests by preserving the existing DSL, with the repeated rationale that Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pd1max, and related quantities are external operating-condition or capacity inputs. The request guidance itself forbade inventing internal plant/environment dynamics merely to make external input variables appear written.

The DSL diff is intentionally empty. That is acceptable here because the diagnostics are non-hard, waiver-allowed design warnings, and textual edits such as self-assignments, constant guard simplification, or deleting guards would reduce NL fidelity by damaging the required twelve-state logical selector behavior.

No regression is indicated: local evidence reports regression_detected=false and drift_risk=none, and there are no scenario failures in the pre-scenario summary. The candidate also retains the overload illegal state behavior, low-SoC charging margins Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10, RES charging/spare behavior, battery/LNG/DG priority branches, and cut-in/cut-out command assignments.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 rejected the candidate for design_target_unresolved, specifically W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR on Pd2max and Pbdismax and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE on forced transition guards whose variables are external inputs/capacity bounds. This is a conservative design diagnostic rather than evidence of NL noncompliance: the NL says the FSM reads these inputs and capacity bounds; it does not require or describe EMS-internal writes to them.

Adding writes to Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, or Pd1max would invent environment/plant dynamics and violate the request's forbidden edits. Adding meaningless self-assignments would only silence the diagnostic without modeling a real EMS behavior. Simplifying guards to literals or removing them would delete the NL-required logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.

The SL-9 rationale resolves the remembered design objections by explicitly reclassifying the warned variables as read-only external inputs and preserving the forced-transition classifier abstraction. Because all required DSL elements remain represented and local evidence shows no regression or drift, the unresolved local warnings are overridden for the next top-down revalidation pass.

The candidate preserves all twelve required states, the required variables, the required forced selection guards, and the required dispatch actions/commands.

The request guidance itself forbade inventing internal plant/environment dynamics merely to make external input variables appear written.

The DSL diff is intentionally empty. That is acceptable here because the diagnostics are non-hard, waiver-allowed design warnings, and textual edits such as self-assignments, constant guard simplification, or deleting guards would reduce NL fidelity by damaging the required twelve-state logical selector behavior.

The candidate also retains the overload illegal state behavior, low-SoC charging margins Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10, RES charging/spare behavior, battery/LNG/DG priority branches, and cut-in/cut-out command assignments.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 rejected the candidate for design_target_unresolved, specifically W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR on Pd2max and Pbdismax and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE on forced transition guards whose variables are external inputs/capacity bounds. This is a conservative design diagnostic rather than evidence of NL noncompliance: the NL says the FSM reads these inputs and capacity bounds; it does not require or describe EMS-internal writes to them.

Adding writes to Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, or Pd1max would invent environment/plant dynamics and violate the request's forbidden edits. Adding meaningless self-assignments would only silence the diagnostic without modeling a real EMS behavior. Simplifying guards to literals or removing them would delete the NL-required logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.

The SL-9 rationale resolves the remembered design objections by explicitly reclassifying the warned variables as read-only external inputs and preserving the forced-transition classifier abstraction. Because all required DSL elements remain represented and local evidence shows no regression or drift, the unresolved local warnings are overridden for the next top-down revalidation pass.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve Pd2max as an external input/read-only capacity bound; do not invent internal writes.']
decisions.rationale: Pd2max is an external DG2 capacity bound used to classify dispatch branches. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds/resources; it does not define EMS-internal dynamics that update DG2 capacity. A DSL write would be a meaningless self-assignment or invented plant dynamics, so the safe repair is conservative preservation with explicit grounding rationale.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve Pbdismax as an external input/read-only capacity bound; do not invent internal writes.']
decisions.rationale: Pbdismax is an external battery-discharge capacity bound needed by the NL priority logic. The NL does not specify EMS-internal update semantics for this bound. Adding a write would be ungrounded, so the safe repair is conservative preservation with explicit grounding rationale.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve BatteryOnly guard as an external-input logical selector.']
decisions.rationale: The BatteryOnly selection guard reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbdismax, all of which are external demand/resource/battery-condition inputs in the NL. The guard is the required logical state selector and should not be simplified or replaced by invented updates.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve BatteryLng guard as an external-input logical selector.']
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLng guard encodes the NL priority of RES, suitable battery discharge, then LNG before diesel using external inputs and capacity bounds. No NL-grounded internal writes exist for these inputs.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve BatteryLngDg1 guard as an external-input logical selector.']
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLngDg1 guard is required to represent the later priority branch where DG1 is used after battery and LNG capacity are insufficient. Its variables are external inputs/capacity bounds, so adding writes would be ungrounded.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve AllThermalNormalSoc guard as an external-input logical selector.']
decisions.rationale: The AllThermalNormalSoc guard uses external demand, renewable, battery, and thermal-capacity values to select the all-thermal normal-SoC branch. This is a required NL branch and should remain condition-driven.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc guard as an external-input logical selector.']
decisions.rationale: The LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc guard represents the NL low-SoC diesel-generator case with Pd1max/10 charging margin and DG2 last priority. The read variables are external conditions/capacity bounds; internal writes would invent dynamics.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve OverloadCompletionIllegal guard as an external-input logical selector.']
decisions.rationale: The OverloadCompletionIllegal guard is required by the NL to represent the illegal overload-completion branch where all thermal units are active and remaining lack is covered by battery discharge. Its inputs are external operating conditions/capacity bounds.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve forced transition expansion behavior and external-input guard.']
decisions.rationale: The ZeroLoadSpare-to-BatteryOnly expanded forced guard warning is another instance of the same external-input classifier. PL/Ppv/Pw/SoC/Pbdismax are read from the environment/resources and are not EMS-internal state variables.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve forced transition expansion behavior and external-input guard.']
decisions.rationale: The ZeroLoadSpare-to-BatteryLng expanded guard is NL-grounded dispatch selection over external demand/resource/capacity inputs. Adding writes would be meaningless and forbidden by the request guidance.

diff_summary.summary: No DSL text changed. The repair is a conservative design-level acceptance/grounding response: preserve external-input guards and read-only capacity bounds rather than adding ungrounded writes or deleting required twelve-state dispatch logic.

repair_rationale: No textual DSL edit is the smallest safe repair. The selected diagnostics are W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE on variables that the NL defines as read inputs: PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, engine/generator capacity bounds, and battery-discharge capacity.

The NL requires the twelve states to be selected by logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC. Replacing those guards with constants or removing them would delete required behavior.

Adding writes to Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, or Pd1max would invent plant/environment dynamics that the NL does not provide and is specifically forbidden by the repair request guidance.

All required preserved states, variables, and key selection transitions remain represented. The model remains a guarded condition-classifier EMS over externally supplied operating conditions and writes only EMS outputs/commands.

variable_role_summary.policy: Advisory only. Do not invent writes for external_input_candidate variables unless NL explicitly gives update semantics; add meaningful NL-grounded writes only for internal state variables.
variable_role_summary.source: SD-4 diagnostic refs and generic NL external-input rationale

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve Pd2max as a read-only external capacity input and keep the NL-grounded guards unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Pd2max is an externally read DG2 capacity bound required by the NL's capacity-based dispatch selection. The FixLog shows the same local warning was already overridden by SL-10 because adding an EMS-internal write would invent plant/capacity dynamics or create a meaningless self-assignment.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve Pbdismax as a read-only external capacity input and avoid ungrounded writes.
decisions.rationale: Pbdismax is an externally read battery discharge capacity bound needed for the battery-priority and overload branch guards. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds; it does not define internal updates to those bounds.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve BatteryOnly guard as an external-input logical state selector.
decisions.rationale: The BatteryOnly selection guard over PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbdismax is a required logical condition over external load/resource/SoC/capacity inputs. Simplifying or rewriting it would damage the twelve-state classifier required by the NL.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve BatteryLng guard and dispatch behavior.
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLng guard implements the required priority order RES first, suitable battery discharge, then LNG before diesel, using external demand/resource and capacity values. No NL-grounded internal update exists for those inputs.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve BatteryLngDg1 guard as an NL-grounded capacity selector.
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLngDg1 guard is needed for the branch where battery and LNG capacity are insufficient and DG1 is introduced before DG2. Its variables are external operating conditions and capacity bounds.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve AllThermalNormalSoc guard and output actions.
decisions.rationale: The AllThermalNormalSoc guard selects the branch using all thermal units at normal SoC, based on external demand, renewable contribution, battery capacity, and thermal capacity. Deleting or constant-folding it would violate the NL.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc low-SoC guard.
decisions.rationale: The LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc guard represents the required low-SoC diesel-generator branch with the Pd1max/10 charging margin and DG2 as last priority. The warning arises because pyfcstm cannot know these are external inputs.

accepted_edit_intent: Preserve OverloadCompletionIllegal guard and actions.
decisions.rationale: The OverloadCompletionIllegal guard is required by the NL to represent the illegal overload completion case where all thermal units are active and the remaining lack is battery discharge. It must remain condition-selected by external operating inputs.

diff_summary.summary: No textual DSL edit. Preserve the existing NL-grounded condition-classifier FSM and treat the warned read-only capacity/demand/resource variables as external inputs rather than inventing ungrounded writes.

repair_rationale: The smallest safe edit is intentionally no DSL text change. The current model already represents the NL-required twelve states, required external input variables, required output variables/commands, RES charge/spare behavior, battery/LNG/DG priority branches, low-SoC Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 margins, and the illegal overload completion branch.

The selected warnings are W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for Pd2max and Pbdismax and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE for forced classifier guards. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not specify EMS-internal dynamics that update those inputs.

Adding writes to Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, or Pd1max would violate the request's forbidden edits by inventing plant/environment dynamics. Self-assignments would be meaningless. Simplifying guards to constants or deleting guards would remove the required logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.

The FixLog was read completely: iteration 0 made the same conservative decision, SD-10 local warnings were explicitly overridden by SL-10, and repair_memory contains no new actionable rework guidance or regression evidence. Therefore the unchanged DSL with explicit external-input grounding remains the non-regressive NL-faithful candidate.

local_override_rationale: The remembered repair_memory objections concerned SD-10 design_target_unresolved warnings: W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR on Pd2max and Pbdismax and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE on guards over external input variables. Those objections were already overridden in iteration 0 because the NL requires these values to be read as operating conditions/capacity bounds and the request guidance forbids inventing internal writes. The current candidate is the same non-regressive DSL and current local evidence no longer reports an unresolved target, so the remembered objections remain resolved by the prior audited external-input rationale rather than by textual mutation.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve Pd2max as a read-only external capacity input and keep the NL-grounded guards unchanged.']
decisions.rationale: Pd2max is an externally read DG2 capacity bound required by the NL's capacity-based dispatch selection. The FixLog shows the same local warning was already overridden by SL-10 because adding an EMS-internal write would invent plant/capacity dynamics or create a meaningless self-assignment.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve Pbdismax as a read-only external capacity input and avoid ungrounded writes.']
decisions.rationale: Pbdismax is an externally read battery discharge capacity bound needed for the battery-priority and overload branch guards. The NL says the FSM reads capacity bounds; it does not define internal updates to those bounds.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve BatteryOnly guard as an external-input logical state selector.']
decisions.rationale: The BatteryOnly selection guard over PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbdismax is a required logical condition over external load/resource/SoC/capacity inputs. Simplifying or rewriting it would damage the twelve-state classifier required by the NL.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve BatteryLng guard and dispatch behavior.']
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLng guard implements the required priority order RES first, suitable battery discharge, then LNG before diesel, using external demand/resource and capacity values. No NL-grounded internal update exists for those inputs.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve BatteryLngDg1 guard as an NL-grounded capacity selector.']
decisions.rationale: The BatteryLngDg1 guard is needed for the branch where battery and LNG capacity are insufficient and DG1 is introduced before DG2. Its variables are external operating conditions and capacity bounds.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve AllThermalNormalSoc guard and output actions.']
decisions.rationale: The AllThermalNormalSoc guard selects the branch using all thermal units at normal SoC, based on external demand, renewable contribution, battery capacity, and thermal capacity. Deleting or constant-folding it would violate the NL.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc low-SoC guard.']
decisions.rationale: The LngDg1Dg2ChargeLowSoc guard represents the required low-SoC diesel-generator branch with the Pd1max/10 charging margin and DG2 as last priority. The warning arises because pyfcstm cannot know these are external inputs.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve OverloadCompletionIllegal guard and actions.']
decisions.rationale: The OverloadCompletionIllegal guard is required by the NL to represent the illegal overload completion case where all thermal units are active and the remaining lack is battery discharge. It must remain condition-selected by external operating inputs.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve forced transition classifier behavior.']
decisions.rationale: The ZeroLoadSpare-to-BatteryOnly warning is an expanded instance of the global forced transition classifier. The guard remains correct because it reads external load, renewable, SoC, and battery capacity values.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve external-input BatteryLng forced-selection guard.']
decisions.rationale: The ZeroLoadSpare-to-BatteryLng warning is also an expanded forced-transition guard over external EMS inputs. Adding writes would invent plant dynamics and removing the guard would remove a required dispatch branch.

diff_summary.summary: No textual DSL edit. Preserve the existing NL-grounded condition-classifier FSM and treat the warned read-only capacity/demand/resource variables as external inputs rather than inventing ungrounded writes.

repair_rationale: The smallest safe edit is intentionally no DSL text change. The current model already represents the NL-required twelve states, required external input variables, required output variables/commands, RES charge/spare behavior, battery/LNG/DG priority branches, low-SoC Pgmax/5 and Pd1max/10 margins, and the illegal overload completion branch.

The selected warnings are W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for Pd2max and Pbdismax and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE for forced classifier guards. The NL explicitly says the FSM reads PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds; it does not specify EMS-internal dynamics that update those inputs.

Adding writes to Pd2max, Pbdismax, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, or Pd1max would violate the request's forbidden edits by inventing plant/environment dynamics. Self-assignments would be meaningless. Simplifying guards to constants or deleting guards would remove the required logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.

The FixLog was read completely: iteration 0 made the same conservative decision, SD-10 local warnings were explicitly overridden by SL-10, and repair_memory contains no new actionable rework guidance or regression evidence. Therefore the unchanged DSL with explicit external-input grounding remains the non-regressive NL-faithful candidate.
